text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"SQLite has offered WAL mode since version 3.7.0.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 states that beginning with version 3.7.0, a new Write-Ahead Log option is available.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new \"Write-Ahead Log\" option (hereafter referred to as \"WAL\") is available."}]},{"claim_text":"In WAL mode, writers and readers can run at the same time.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 directly states writers and readers can run at the same time.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of readers, writers and readers can run at the same time."}]},{"claim_text":"In WAL mode, there can only be one writer at a time.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 directly states there can only be one writer at a time.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time."}]},{"claim_text":"A checkpoint runs automatically once the WAL file reaches 1000 pages.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 states that by default SQLite automatically checkpoints when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages."}]},{"claim_text":"The WAL file is normally named after the database file with a \"-wal\" suffix.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 states the WAL file name is usually the database file name with an extra \"-wal\" suffix.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"The name of this file on disk is usually the name of the database file with an extra \"-wal\" suffix"}]}]}
